subject.title: [Bug]: Ctrl+C not working in Windows install on foreground

question: Should repair work wait until a native Windows npm-global Ctrl+C repro identifies whether signal delivery or gateway shutdown is failing?
rationale: Current source already handles delivered SIGINT, and the only linked fix branch was closed unmerged, so automation cannot safely choose the fix layer without native Windows proof.

options.title: Require Windows live repro
options.body: Keep this issue open for a Windows-capable maintainer or reporter to validate current main or the latest package in PowerShell, cmd.exe, and Windows Terminal before repair work starts.

options.title: Queue after delivery proof
options.body: If live proof shows Ctrl+C is not delivered to Node, queue a narrow stdin or wrapper fix with terminal-state cleanup coverage and Windows package proof.

options.title: Treat existing SIGINT code as sufficient
options.body: Close only if a native Windows run shows Ctrl+C now reaches the current process handler and shuts the gateway down cleanly.

recommendation.title: Require Windows live repro
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a Windows-capable maintainer or reporter to validate current main or the latest package in PowerShell, cmd.exe, and Windows Terminal before repair work starts.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated gateway CLI lifecycle and docs work near this foreground command path.
